common_name: Pink Frost Fortune's Eupatorium (Variegated Fragrant Boneset)

planting.note: Divide and transplant in spring once new shoots emerge, into humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in full sun to light shade; foliage variegation and pink blush intensify with more sun and cooler weather.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist but drains well, siting in full sun for the boldest pink-and-cream leaf margins or light afternoon shade in hotter climates. This East Asian species (a relative of the North American native boneset and Joe-Pye weeds) forms an upright clump of lance-shaped, three-lobed leaves broadly edged in creamy white with a pink flush that deepens as nights cool in autumn. Fluffy mauve-pink flower clusters open in late summer into fall atop the foliage, drawing butterflies and other pollinators even as the variegated leaves remain the main ornamental draw. Cut the clump back hard in late winter before new growth emerges, and divide every three to four years to maintain vigor and the best variegation.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden
